newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices retreat with futures.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices retreat with futures.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices were on the retreat Wednesday, mirroring the declining futures market, traders said.

NYMEX's September contract extended its losses to reach a low of $2.405, down from the contract high of $2.605 set earlier this week. At 1342 EDT, however, September recovered to $2.485, up one cent from Tuesday's settlement.

On the Louisiana Gulf Coast, swing prices at the Henry Hub were down an average of 11 cents to the high-$2.30s early and the high-$2.40s shortly before nomination deadlines. Most deals were reported done at $2.43-2.45.
In the Midwest, swing prices dropped about 10 cents to the mid-$2.30s. Chicago city-gate gas prices were also quoted sharply lower in the high-$2.40s to mid-$2.50s.
In the Permian Basin market, prices lost 13 cents to the mid-to-high $2.30s.

El Paso's Keystone Mainline Station, in Winkler County, Texas, will be down through Thursday for maintenance, affecting about 400 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) at the receipt points in the Permian Basin and about 185 mmcfd of supply at Waha.
Southern California border prices retreated by 13 cents to the low-$2.40s.
In the East, prices at the New York city gate also fell at least 10 cents to the low-$2.60s.
According to a Reuter poll, injection estimates for today's American Gas Association storage report have ranged from 70 to 80 bcf.
